note: The v1.1 simulation's central negative result: DEF-1 factivity and the v1.1 attribution equation K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable for any total attributing Gamma, established by an explicit witness (two worlds, same epistemic state, different truth, e.g. attributed os=RHEL9.8 vs true RHEL8.6) and confirmed at scale (420/10000 randomized trials, 414/665 violations when a policy-trusted source reports a falsehood, 0/2607 otherwise). Three unchosen repairs (R1 rename K_t, R2 externalize factivity, R3 partial Gamma) are registered in the theory gap register.

The v1.1 circularity audit's one genuine finding: semantic equivalence (P7) is defined via a behavioural projection chosen by the experimenter, and behaviour is compared under that same projection -- circular and unresolved, and declared blocking for any kernel-minimality claim (it is why the prior kernel-reduction lane found 13 operators under one algebra and 8 under another). Candidate independent grounding: fix the theory's epistemic preservation vector P=(Meaning,Evidence,Warrant,Uncertainty,Alternatives,History,Identity,Context,Inquiry,Authorization) by contract and define equivalence as agreement on its declared-essential dimensions -- not tested.

CIRC-3 finding: Adequate (DEF-20) and Zero (DEF-22) are extensionally identical in the v1.1 theory -- both reduce to the same emptiness-of-Delta_t condition, and Adequate's implementation is literally 'return Zero(...)' -- a redundancy, not a circularity, with two possible repairs (derive one from the other and say so, or give Adequate independent content such as a degree or a subset-relative reading) left open.

notations: world-contact, evidential admission, meaning assignment, hypothesis-space opening, target-relative assessment, set-valued selection, elimination, attribution, state commit, normative comparison, closure judgment, action preference, authorization
note: The v1.1 kernel-result artifact's thirteen externally-distinguishable semantic capabilities (each shown to have an observable behaviour separating a system with it from one without), plus seven candidate reductions tested: Adequate<-Zero SUPPORTED (redundant), and six others (Determination<-Knowledge, Decision<-Determination, Authorization<-Decision, Action<-Authorization, Underdetermined<-Unobservable, Evidence<-Observation) all REFUTED by explicit counterexample. No operator-count minimality is claimed; distinguishability is called necessary but not sufficient for irreducibility, and CIRC-5 blocks any semantic-minimality claim until equivalence is independently grounded.

The v1.1 simulation's thirteen-item classified gap register (TG-1..TG-13, each tagged with a G1-G9 gap class and severity), covering the factivity impossibility, missing evidence-retirement relation, Adequate/Zero redundancy, circular semantic equivalence, the E/EpistemicState notation collision, empty-provenance attribution, unproved exhaustiveness of requirement kinds/unknown taxonomy, whether attribution is epistemics-or-governance, unstructured uncertainty, the synthetic-world empirical limit, constructed-not-acquired observation tokens, a table-lookup authorization model, and the untested prior-lane kernel shape (P,R,delta,I,U).

The v1.1 simulation's final verdict: Theory Status B -- PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE. The full epistemic lifecycle (Reality->Observation->Evidence->...->Action->O_{t+1}) executes and every declared distinction survives except one: DEF-1 factivity and the v1.1 attribution equation cannot both hold. Explicitly not A (inconsistent, since the contradiction is localized and three repairs exist), not C, and not D (tests passing is explicitly not the reason). Kernel status: NOT TESTED, deliberately, per the protocol's ban on operator counting and CIRC-5's block on minimality claims. Next experiment prescribed: the Factivity Repair Experiment (R1/R2/R3 as three arms over the same 10000 worlds).

CE-3: the v1.1 theory's Revise operator leaves superseded evidence at full weight because no evidence-retirement relation exists (Supersede/Retract/Expire are named in the corpus but unmodelled), which drives a changing world monotonically toward permanent underdetermination -- classified a theory gap (TG-2, semantic class, HIGH severity), not an implementation defect, and persists unrepaired under v1.2 as well.

A same-day methodological correction memo arguing Theory v1.1 should not be treated as closed: it proposes a constitutional four-layer separation (Philosophical/Conceptual -> Epistemic Mathematical -> DDD Domain -> Architectural Realization) forbidding direct Gita-concept-to-architecture inference, downgrades several v1.1 constructs (K_t's operational completeness, Observation's tuple definition, Buddhi, Sarathi, Zero, the transformation equation) from established to candidate/open/lens status, introduces an 11-item epistemic status vocabulary (ESTABLISHED..UNKNOWN), reframes Steps 286-290's individual purposes, and proposes a restructured Theory v1.2 table of contents plus a claim-by-claim v1.1-to-v1.2 reconciliation matrix as the next research act.

The v1.2 simulation lane (artifacts A-E plus FINAL-VERDICT), reusing the v1.1 pipeline unchanged and replacing only the evaluation layer with class-indexed three-valued Sat:K x R -> {T,F,U} over eight requirement classes, so that any v1.1/v1.2 difference is attributable to the theory rather than the simulator. Five experiments (E1-E5) test whether the weakened v1.2 theory repairs, worsens, or merely re-diagnoses the v1.1 failures.

E1's central finding: under three-valued class-indexed Sat, 'Zero iff Delta_t=empty' names three non-equivalent predicates (Zero_strict, Zero_weak, Zero_kleene) that disagree on the most favourable case -- a fully determined, corroborated state is strict=false, weak=true, Kleene=U -- because the three universally-open classes (governance, temporal, operational) supply every U, so Zero cannot be evaluated until they are closed (Step 261's meta-gate reappearing independently). Zero_strict is unreachable in every case tested across the whole v1.2 lane.

notations: state, missingness representation, relation, predicate, boundary, derived view, metaphor
note: E5's test of Zero's seven v1.2-declared candidate readings: 'state' and 'missingness representation' REFUTED (Zero is computed from (K,Req) and stored in no K; all four unknown kinds collapse to the single value U, so Zero is coarser than the missingness taxonomy); 'relation' PARTIAL; 'predicate' and 'boundary' SUPPORTED with conditions (arity/value-set contested; boundary only holds under three-valued Sat); 'derived view' SUPPORTED; 'metaphor' NOT REFUTED. The status-classification artifact records the vocabulary's own gap: no term exists for 'refuted as one reading, surviving as another.'

E2's finding that v1.2's five non-substitutable equality/identity relations actually form a partial implication order (struct_eq => prov_equiv => sem_equiv => obs_equiv, and struct_eq => identity) in 7 of 20 ordered pairs, with the remaining 13 genuinely non-substitutable -- refining v1.2's blanket 'no one may silently substitute for another' into a directional rule. The order itself is shown to be lambda-relative: sem=>obs holds for lambda=(status,value) or (A) but fails when lambda contains provenance or weight.

The Factivity Repair Experiment: re-runs the same 10000 worlds under three named repairs plus a corrected R3'. R1 (rename K_t to AttributedState) and R2 (externalize factivity to an outside verifier) are behaviourally identical and both genuinely repair factivity by construction, at the cost of vocabulary/an added component -- R2's extra benefit is making a measurable 88.25% external-verification survival rate visible. R3 as specified (partial Gamma restricted to verifiable properties) does NOT repair factivity (0.1181 vs baseline 0.1175) while costing 66% of coverage, because verifiability-by-availability is not verifiability-by-warrant. A corrected R3' (which actually consults the verification channel) reaches zero violations only by ceasing to be a function of evidence alone -- 71.2% of its attributions are not products of the epistemic pipeline -- so it escapes the impossibility theorem by leaving its hypotheses, not by refuting it.

notations: R_content, R_evidence, R_provenance, R_status, R_consistency, R_governance, R_temporal, R_operational
note: The originating proposal (and its two nested self-reviews) for a class-indexed, three-valued satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r) in {top,bot,U}, defined separately per eight requirement classes (content, evidence, provenance, epistemic-status, consistency, governance, temporal, operational) with Kleene-conjunctive composition for composite requirements, explicitly kept at candidate/[PROP] status pending a Factivity Repair Experiment, and later downgraded further to treat Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal as the primary object with Sat_c only a tested projection.

The Sat_c Semantic Closure Experiment: specifying (not implementing) the eight Sat_c classes already exposes that only 3 of 8 (content, evidence, provenance) are executable -- status/consistency/governance/temporal/operational are blocked by named missing evaluators (A-1) -- and that no class in the family requires factivity at all, so a state can satisfy all eight and still be false (A-2), locating CE-1's cause in the satisfaction family's structure rather than in Gamma. Adversarial testing then finds Sat_content is not total under contradiction (PB-2), the declared U-reason vocabulary is incomplete (PB-3), blocked-class contagion makes every composite requirement of arity>=4 permanently U (PB-4), and operational satisfaction is not provably well-founded (PB-5). Introduces a fourth Zero reading, Zero_reasoned (closes on non-agent-remediable U only), and the derived chain Zero_strict => Zero_reasoned => Zero_weak.

A fourth candidate Zero closure reading -- Zero_reasoned(g) iff no requirement is bot and no U-valued requirement remains that the agent itself could still act on -- introduced in the Sat_c Semantic Closure Experiment as genuinely distinct from Zero_weak (separating case: content=U/nobody-has-looked-yet closes weak but not reasoned) and later derived (not merely observed) to sit strictly between Zero_strict and Zero_weak in an implication chain, though its practical separation from Zero_weak was subsequently found to be an artifact of invented (corpus-unsupported) governance/temporal evaluators once those were retracted.

Artifact H: enumerates and tests (without choosing) candidate repairs for PB-2 (four contradiction-codomain candidates; only R_b -- delegate content to consistency -- is total, three-valued and preserves absence!=negation, but it creates a dependency on the still-undefined consistency class), PB-3 (only a skeleton-derived three-structural-source reason taxonomy could be provably exhaustive; enumeration cannot be), and PB-5 (stratifying Sat_op into levels is the only candidate that terminates, keeps expressiveness, and makes well-foundedness failure visible in the value). Also upgrades the Zero_strict=>Zero_reasoned=>Zero_weak chain from observed to machine-checked derived (1,620,000 assignments, 0 counterexamples), and shows the earlier -E evaluator run understated blocked-class contagion because it ran before the PB-2 repair (arity-2 contagion corrected from 0.464 to 0.643).

A full rewritten commissioning prompt for the next Sat_c/evaluation-semantics experiment (renaming the primary object Eval_c->EVal with Sat_c only a tested projection, listing PB-2/PB-3/PB-4/PB-5 as binding predecessor findings, ten required negative tests N1-N10, eight epistemic-discipline rules such as 'no invented semantics' and 'closure is not truth', and eight STOP conditions), paired with a self-review concluding the previously-proposed Zero Closure Decision Experiment is premature and should be replaced by a four-step sequence: I Contradiction/Consistency semantics, II Epistemic Status Order, III Evaluation Semantics, IV Zero Closure -- and walking back the prior claim that 'Zero is the closure predicate of the whole theory' to 'Zero functions as a candidate closure predicate in the tested model; canonical status remains OPEN.'

The evaluator-supplied rerun of Phases B and C with experimenter-invented governance/temporal/operational evaluators: contagion roughly halves at low arity but is unchanged at arity 7-8; Zero_strict remains unreachable (0/80) unless the experimenter also invents the status ordering and contradiction predicate (then 1/80); Zero_reasoned fires on 8/80 vs Zero_weak's 36/80, and the reason-bucket partition needed two new categories (governance-remediable, normative-decision) it did not have. Later self-retracted: Eval_Gov and Eval_Time were corpus-unsupported invented semantics (violating the commissioning rules), and once removed, the Zero_reasoned/Zero_weak separation collapses to an artifact -- the two readings agree on every honest case in the suite.

D-0: all four candidate Zero readings (strict/weak/reasoned/Kleene) test only for the values bot and U, so a state holding both p and not-p is declared epistemically closed under three different contradiction-codomain models (three-valued UNDEFINED, four-valued C, delegated U/NO_EVALUATOR) alike -- not because the models agree, but because none of the readings can see any value outside {top,bot,U}. Extending the codomain to represent contradiction therefore requires extending every Zero definition in the same step, or closure will silently swallow the new value.

The consolidated Sat_c/evaluation-semantics experiment (final, ID-collision-corrected as -G): establishes Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal_c as the primary object with Sat_c:=value-of-Eval_c a tested (not assumed) projection; finds the three-valued content evaluator not total (undefined on contradiction), and that value-of-Eval_c collapses nine semantically distinct evaluation situations into the single value U (A6, refuting the sufficiency of a three-valued codomain); retracts two prior invented evaluators (Eval_Gov, Eval_Time) as corpus-unsupported; runs eight falsification tests N1-N10, refuting eight of ten; and delivers the final SAT STATUS verdict 'SEMANTICALLY INCOHERENT' under the theory's currently-proposed model (not merely partially executable), because the content evaluator is not a function on contradictory states and the value projection destroys distinctions the theory's own Rule 3 requires.

The candidate reformulation of Zero away from a truth-valued closure predicate toward an inquiry/context/lens-relative examination operation ZeroLens(K_t,I_t,Gamma_t,L_t) -> Boundary_t that exposes what a knowledge representation establishes, does not establish, and may fail to represent, while explicitly not itself being a knowledge element, a truth value, a decision, an authorization, or a state-mutating operation. Developed across a chain of self-reviewing drafts into a frozen 'Zero Concept v1.2' formulation.

The constitutional separation, repeatedly re-derived and re-affirmed across this research thread, between Zero Lens (ZL(K,I,Gamma,L)->Boundary, an examination operation, candidate-status [PROP]-strongly-supported) and Zero Closure (whether a boundary constitutes epistemic closure for a given inquiry, remaining [OPEN] and dependent on unresolved evaluation/status-ordering/contradiction/temporal semantics) -- retiring the earlier 'Zero iff Delta_t=empty' as a Zero-Lens definition while allowing 'ZeroClosure iff Delta^sem_t=empty' to survive only as an open hypothesis.

notations: Do not collapse semantically distinct boundary conditions merely because they share a coarse projection
note: The proposed mathematical/conceptual core of the whole Zero programme, generalizing the ten individual non-collapse invariants into one meta-principle: distinct epistemic boundary conditions (contradiction, absence, evidence insufficiency, unobservability, underdetermination, theory incompleteness, etc.) must not be identified with one another merely because a downstream evaluator projects them to the same coarse value (e.g. all to U).

Ten candidate Zero non-collapse invariants: ZI-01 Unknown!=Absent, ZI-02 NotAssessed!=LowConfidence, ZI-03 NotApplicable!=Unknown, ZI-04 NoEvidence!=InvalidEvidence, ZI-05 Unresolved!=False, ZI-06 UnknownDimension!=UnknownValue, ZI-07 Representation!=Reality, ZI-08 PreviouslyUnknown!=PreviouslyAbsent, ZI-09 Conflict!=Invalidity, ZI-10 NoKnownGap!=Complete -- later tested against an eleven-facet typed-boundary vocabulary and found only partially testable/expressible (ZI-07 and ZI-10 have no facet to live in; 7 of 10 untestable against a 9-state suite).

A candidate 'boundary-of-boundary' hypothesis (kept explicitly [PROP], out of the minimal Zero definition): a lens L_i produces a representation R_i of an object O, and MetaZero examines the lens itself to characterize classes of things it could systematically fail to discover -- distinguished from ordinary boundary detection because it requires a model of the lens, not just of the current representation, and explicitly not solved by the mathematics establishing that Zero cannot compute D*-D_t when D* is itself unknown.

The recurring central hypothesis that the coarse evaluation value U is a lossy, many-to-one projection pi of a richer boundary-condition set B (b1 != b2 but pi(b1)=pi(b2)=U), so the correct discipline is to preserve B first and project to a value only when a downstream consumer needs one -- reached independently from two directions (the Zero Lens document's own derivation and Experiment G's A6 measurement of nine distinct evaluation situations collapsing into one U), which the corpus explicitly classifies as corroboration, not derivation.

The frozen 37/38-section 'KnowledgeOS Zero Concept v1.2' write-up (status [PROP], produced against an explicit review): Zero is redefined as a disciplined, inquiry-relative boundary examination (not a knowledge element, not a truth value, not a decision, not an authorization mechanism, not itself three-valued, non-mutating, and re-applicable rather than inherently infinite-recursive), carrying the ten ZI non-collapse invariants, a MetaZero hypothesis kept out of the core definition, an explicit anti-reification/anti-hallucination reading (Representation!=Reality; NotIdentified(X) does not imply X is irrelevant), and a closing 'ZERO PRINCIPLE': what is not represented is not thereby nonexistent.

Artifact I: implementing ZL(K,I,Gamma,L)->B with typed boundary conditions {NotEstablished, Conflict, Unrepresentable, TheoryIncomplete} and defining closure over the boundary (not the value) repairs D-0 in 6 of 6 contradiction-bearing cases under all three tested contradiction models, correcting Experiment G's claim that the codomain choice and the closure question are inseparable; also finds Gap=pi_Q(Boundary) exactly in cardinality but attribute-lossy (loses 'kind' and 'remediable_by'), converging with the independent kernel-reduction lane's finding that DetectGap is derivable, not primitive; and tiers nine Gita/Vedic-derived candidate correspondences (G-1..G-9) by a T0-T4 scale, with Zero-as-non-collapse (G-5) the only one to reach a testable, passing, self-correcting prediction, and Atman-as-Ideal-State (G-8) explicitly refuted as architecturally out of scope.

The Boundary Separation Experiment: shows nine adversarial epistemic conditions (contradiction, absence, evidence-insufficiency, unobservable, underdetermined, theory-incomplete, agent-remediable, not-applicable, not-assessed) all project to the single value U yet remain pairwise distinct when represented as facet-tagged boundaries (0/36 collisions) -- but an anti-rigging test on facet keys alone finds 1 collision inside the critical six (EvidenceInsufficiency vs Underdetermined, both touching the same three facets) and an exhaustive 2^11 search finds no facet-key subset separates them; a three-value typed vocabulary for one facet (G_assessment) repairs it. Also finds 4 of 11 facets and 7 of 10 ZI invariants untestable by the nine-state suite.

Artifact K: specifies a provenance-tagged typed vocabulary of 35 condition-types across 11 boundary facets, tests it against an 18-state/153-pair extended suite (0 collisions, all facets exercised), then runs a parsimony audit finding only 2 of 11 facets (G_assessment, G_model) actually need internal typing and only 4 of 41 declared type-distinctions are load-bearing on this suite (37 rest on provenance alone, unsupported by evidence) -- correcting Experiment J's claim of a single minimal three-facet repair by finding two size-three minimal sufficient typing sets, both requiring G_assessment and G_model. Also re-confirms boundary-based Zero closure is invariant across all three contradiction models.

A state-of-research synthesis re-deriving the current Zero Lens/Zero Closure separation and laying out an eight-track TODO roadmap (close Zero Lens semantics; define what a Boundary object is without turning it into architecture; test the B->projection/U-is-lossy hypothesis; run a contradiction/identity/temporal-semantics experiment only after boundary semantics are tested; revisit Eval/Sat after Zero; treat Zero Closure as strictly downstream; keep MetaZero and TryBest as later, non-priority tracks), plus an explicit do-not-yet list (no ZeroAggregate, no BoundaryAggregate, no implemented Sat_c, no fourth truth value, no Zero>Sat claim, no kernel membership for Zero).

A philosophical-brainstorming thread applying Jacob Meskin's speculative sexual/yoni interpretation of mathematical zero (from the book Finding Zero) to KnowledgeOS: zero as receptive void/womb generating numbers, extended across several follow-on documents to negative numbers as 'trace of withdrawal', persons in intercourse as complementary knowers/prosecutor-defender-judge in a court of inquiry, and emotions/concentration during intercourse as epistemic states (desire=motivation, confidence=certainty, doubt=uncertainty), culminating in an explicit equation Knowledge = Unknown x Inquiry x Evidence and Unknown-as-the-KnowledgeOS-yoni.

The critical review of the Meskin sexual-metaphor thread: accepts the underlying philosophical intuition (zero as a condition of receptive openness enabling distinction/inquiry) but rejects the literal identification chain Zero=Unknown=empty-set=Shunyata=womb=source-of-knowledge as a category error, explicitly refutes 'Unknown=Zero in KnowledgeOS' against the corpus's own Experiment H findings (heterogeneous boundary conditions collapsing to one U), rejects the equation Knowledge=Unknown x Inquiry x Evidence as undefined/unsupported, and proposes instead mapping the metaphor's 'receptive openness' to the Zero Lens's boundary-examination role while keeping the sexual imagery entirely in the philosophical/[EXT] register.

A proposal modelling the Ideal State as a field of positive (+n, supporting) and negative (-n, opposing) numerically-weighted arguments whose reconciliation (summing to zero) constitutes knowledge/fact, with Fact defined as the infinite-time limit of the knowledge-reconciliation process, elaborated with a full argument algebra (combine/subtract/weight operators) and re-cast through the sexual-yoni metaphor as persons/prosecutor-defender/judge generating and reconciling arguments.

The reviewing decision on the argument-field proposal: rejects 'Knowledge=0'/'IdealState=0' as a universal scalar definition, rejects simple +n/-n numerical weighting as the general epistemic algebra (more evidence != more independent evidence), and rejects Fact=lim(K_t) as unjustified, but extracts and recommends integrating a genuinely new candidate layer -- ArgumentStanding/Reconciliation, sitting between EvidenceAssessment and Determination, representing typed evidential relations (support/oppose/defeat/corroborate/undermine/conflict) hypothesis-space-relative rather than as a bare sum -- registered as candidate AR-01 with three explicit negative constraints (ArgumentStanding!=Knowledge, Reconciliation!=Truth, Zero!=Reconciliation).

An extension of the argument-field/sexual metaphor mapping the two persons in intercourse to two complementary epistemic agents (a proposer generating positive/supporting arguments and a challenger generating negative/opposing arguments) whose union is cast as a court of inquiry (prosecutor/defender/judge/verdict) producing 'new knowledge' as their reconciled offspring, with an explicit non-multiplicative reading of Knowledge = Person A (x) Person B as dynamic interaction rather than arithmetic product.

A reinterpretation of the proposal/challenge/reconciliation sexual metaphor treating 'orgasm' not as a state (rejecting Knowledge=orgasm=balance) but as a discrete ClosureEvent transition K_t -> K_{t+1}, with a worked Nexus-version example and a decisive negative test showing that numeric zero (+a plus -b = 0) is produced by at least six distinct and non-equivalent epistemic conditions (genuine balance, contradiction, insufficiency, incomparability, double-counted dependent evidence, temporally-distinct claims) -- concluding Numeric zero != Epistemic closure, and proposing a falsification-oriented KR-ORGASM research track to test whether Balanced/Reconciled/Determined/Known/Closed can be kept distinct while dynamically linked.

A further extension of the sexual-field metaphor mapping named emotions/feelings during intercourse (desire, anticipation, pleasure, pain, joy, fear, confidence, doubt) and degree of concentration to epistemic states/drives of a knower (motivation to inquire, hope of discovery, satisfaction of understanding, frustration of confusion, achievement, fear of error, certainty, uncertainty, focus-intensity of inquiry), culminating in a final proposed equation Knowledge = Desire x Concentration x Reconciliation.
